I am here in Kigoma, and this maize plot of mine has fed my family for many seasons. I went to school for a few years, enough to read the name on a seed packet and talk sense with the agro-dealer in town, but I still farm like my father taught me. Last season the rains came well enough, and I harvested decent maize, so I will mostly do what I did before. Fertilizer in our area is expensive and the lorry does not always come on time, so I use a little urea when I can find it, top-dressed when the maize is knee-high — maybe one bag of urea across this plot, which works out to a small amount per hectare. I put cattle manure from my own kraal on the parts of the plot closest to the homestead, because carrying it far is hard work. I buy improved maize seed from the agro-dealer because my neighbor Juma has been getting better cobs from it for three seasons now, and the local seed I saved does not yield the same. I do not spray anything — stalk borer comes sometimes but I just pick the worms out or leave it. No irrigation here, we depend on the rains from November. My wife and my two grown sons help me, and at weeding and harvest I pay a few neighbors with food and a little cash to finish on time.
